findings.summary: Whether a callee keeps a callback was decided from the closure's immediate parent, so a closure passed through `as`/`satisfies`/`!`, a conditional arm or `??`/`||`/`&&` still captured caller lets by value; the decision is made at the consuming site, a run-time-chosen closure always gets a shared cell, and an async callee that awaits keeps its called callback parameters (a stored callback that may be undefined now also takes its `??` fallback).
Results computed while an owner's analysis re-entered itself were cached as final; in-cycle answers keep the argument and are not cached.

An asserted closed record copied every member eagerly at the cast, aborting on keys never read and losing later writes; it is a view over the open record's entries that refuses an absent key at the read, with keyed writes through one generated switch per record.

Accessor-capable records paid three allocations per field even for plain data; `Accessor<T>` holds plain data inline (the getter call keeps its snapshot, because a getter replacing its own record would otherwise free its running body).
Every assignment to a class-getter property name paid an extra owner probe; assignments decide from the property's declaration and evaluate the receiver once.
AST-only analysis caches were journaled and dropped on every declined probe; they are plain WeakMaps.
Self-referencing and rebound record promotions were discovered mid-emission and recompiled the file; both are decided in the pre-pass, and the rebinding site no longer marks a type it then refuses.
Call targets restated `EvaluationOrder`'s resolution and four copies tested that every implementation has a body; `EvaluationOrder.callBodies` and `ClassHierarchy.dispatchBodies` serve them.

The stored-accessor setter restated `ClassLowerer.compileSetter` with a new refusal; it calls `compileSetter` inside the record scopes; survey cascades use `rootExpression`; the accessor registry joins the partial-record walk; the docs rows read as facts.
